newsitem.title: USA: Georgia waives immunity for diplomat in U.S. case.
newsitem.headline: Georgia waives immunity for diplomat in U.S. case.

text.p: The former Soviet Republic of Georgia has formally waived immunity so criminal charges can be brought against one of its diplomats involved in a car crash last month that killed a 16-year-old girl, the State Department said on Saturday.

"The government of Georgia has notified the Department of State that it has waived diplomatic immunity for Gueorgui Makharadze," department spokesman Nicholas Burns said in a statement. "We would like to express our appreciation to President (Eduard) Shevardnadze for his decision to take this courageous action," Burns added.

Police say speed and alcohol may have played a role in the Jan. 4 five-car crash, allegedly triggered when Makharadze, travelling at an estimated 80 miles per hour (129 kph), slammed into a car stopped for a red light at Dupont Circle in the heart of Washington.

Prosecutors were expected to seek a grand jury indictment charging him with involuntary manslaughter now that Georgia has waived his immunity. The charges carry a maximum penalty of up to 30 years in prison.

Burns said the State Department would transmit a formal notification of the waiver to the Justice Department on Tuesday. Shevardnadze had announced last month that he was prepared to lift Makharadze's diplomatic immunity so he could face charges if prosecutors decided to file them.
The accident killed Joviane Waltrick, a 16-year-old Brazilian girl living in Kensington, Maryland, a Washington suburb.

Newsweek magazine has reported that tests at Georgetown University hospital, taken several hours after the accident, showed that Makharadze, 35, had a blood alcohol level far above the legally drunk level.

Lawyers close to the case said there have been no discussions between prosecutors and Makharadze's attorneys about a possible plea deal. U.S. Attorney Eric Holder last month wrote to the State Department saying his office believed it had sufficient evidence to prosecute the diplomat if his immunity was waived.
